newsitem.title: FRANCE: Corsican bombs blast electricity utility, villa.
newsitem.headline: Corsican bombs blast electricity utility, villa.

text.p: Two bomb attacks by suspected Corsican separatists blasted a building owned by the French state electricity utility and a holiday home on the Mediterranean island overnight, police said on Sunday.
No one claimed responsibility for the explosions, which caused no casualties.
A small bomb estimated at 150 grammes (five oz) of explosives blew out windows of the EDF electricity utility in Bastia, northern Corsica, late on Saturday night.
Earlier on Saturday, talks had broken down between the EDF and the Communist-led CGT union in a dispute that brought power cuts to the island last week.
The union accuses EDF of failing to implement a 1995 pact to create 20 jobs, while EDF says it has respected the deal.
In southern Corsica, twin bomb blasts on Saturday night wrecked a holiday home in Cala Longa owned by Georges Guerlain, of the French perfume company Guerlain.
No one was in the villa at the time. Guerlain is part of the LVMH Moet Hennessey Louis Vuitton luxury goods group.
